answers.answer: Roll one die for each office card; add one for each fatigue on that card, and the Chairman adds one more. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire the member to Pensioners, flip the office card to Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no card and skip normal office attrition.

Only players who retired at least one pensioner select or discard a display card. They act in descending actual total retirement spending; ties go to most total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from the PM. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace cards during selection; if the display empties, skip all remaining eligible players. Then discard every remaining display card and refill exactly three (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), even if no card was taken. Return all unused Pensioners to supply.

At the start of your Family action, note whether the opportunity marker is on an action. You may take your chosen main action once, or twice if the marker already matched that action; then move the marker onto the chosen action. Only the latest passed extra-action law can grant an additional action afterward; it is not doubled and does not move the marker. With four vacant offices, Enlist Writer adds one extra writer once that turn: a doubled Writer action can therefore place three writers total.

After Family actions, while both Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court as a Company share and lower Debt by one; repeat. If Debt is gone, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order. The initial queue fee is paid from family cash to the bank, never into Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: Family — Seek Share / New Company shares

answers.answer: Fill vacancies in ascending order of the number on each card back. The hirer chooses and moves a candidate into the office; that member’s owner receives the office card. Hiring your own family into an ordinary office requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exceptions. On promotion, move fatigue from the old card to the new card and put the old card into vacant hiring order. If no candidate exists or hirer is vacant, skip it and it stays vacant, with no action or hiring.

The former Chairman first announces how many shares make a pure majority (more than half current shares). Shareholders may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. If nobody does, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. The winner moves one Company share into the Chairman slot; it still counts for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm.

Commit cash from the acting office’s treasury to the bank, gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll; use the lowest die. A 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office-specific limits permit; 5–6 is catastrophic: no more office actions, return the officeholder to supply, discard fatigue and flip the card to Vacant Offices. Specific Commander/firm procedures can modify this. Do not take an action with no effect or chance of success, such as trading without a ship or deploying without dice merely to risk officer losses.

The Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each adding £5 to Balance. Each further advance requires consent of players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting the Chairman; never advance beyond the Debt track end. The Chairman then allocates all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, lowering Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved subject to those limits; money already in office treasuries remains there for their use.

Shipping must spend treasury money until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without its owner’s consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once created. Extra ships return to supply at Refresh.

The President declares the home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from that President’s treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. On success, capacity is one order per ship in that Presidency’s sea zone; ships do not exhaust. Put the first writer in the home port; later orders must extend the route filled in this same Trade. Writers from another Presidency cannot extend it. Use all available writers, then filled-order tokens for remaining ship capacity. Do not fill another President’s home region, even if vacant. Company Balance gains each order’s listed revenue, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn; President gets £1 per order and writer owners £1 per writer placed. Each President may succeed at most once per turn; failures/retries remain that President’s uninterrupted opportunity.

A Commander may target their Presidency’s home, any associated region, or a region bordering an associated region, but not another home or another Presidency’s Company region. A Company target must have unrest or a closed order. Exhaust officers/regiments for one die each and local alliances for printed dice; subtract target strength plus all other regions in its empire, counting target once (Company defense is zero). Roll a normal check; a noncatastrophic failure may retry with remaining resources. After each attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 removes that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll loss checks.

On success, loot is £4 per target tower plus any faceup loot modifier, minimum surviving participating officers + 1 for the Commander. Pay repeated cycles: £1 to Commander plus £1 for each of their used surviving officers; then clockwise families £1 per used surviving officer; bank last £1 per used regiment and per alliance piece. Repeat until distributed; Commander gains one trophy per target tower. Then remove target tower/dome (and all matching flags if it was a capital), open its orders and remove unrest; on new conquest flip loot/control token symbol-side up above the associated President’s box, place Governor overlay in the region, and put only Governor card in Vacant Offices. If Elephant faced outward from target, move it inside. Catastrophe returns half Commander-family trophies rounded up, returns Commander to supply, and exhausted officers still check losses.

Use the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one regardless of result. Success takes £1, or £2 if the immediately previous roll failed, then exactly one benefit: build one stage of a ship, commission a regiment, or Tax. The first successful Build puts a partial ship in the Governor’s region; a later successful Build completes it into the sea zone of that Governor’s President. Commissioned regiments go to that President’s Army. Tax adds an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President’s treasury; each Tax after the first this turn adds unrest in the region. Every unsuccessful roll adds one unrest; catastrophe also removes the officeholder. Continue until stopping, no dice remain, or catastrophe.

Company pays £1 per Debt, Army officer/regiment (not Commander), and sea-zone ship (including China) from Balance. If short, take £5 emergency loans, adding one Debt each, even after the Debt track reaches its maximum; new emergency Debt has no current-turn expense. After loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations at current Standing; if short, lower Standing one. After that the Chairman may pay affordable dividends, one cash per Company share, paying £1 per share to each owner including Chairman. If total dividend cash is strictly greater than expectations, raise Standing one.

Resolve the primary Crisis first, then secondary Rebellions in Company regions with unrest in Bombay, Madras, Bengal Army order; within each Presidency its Commander chooses region order. A primary normal Crisis adds target-region unrest to its normal Invasion/Rebellion attack strength. A primary Foreign Invasion uses only the ordinary attack die. Each secondary Rebellion strength is only that region’s unrest cubes. The associated Commander exhausts Army pieces totaling attack strength, or as much as possible; the printed test says defense succeeds if newly exhausted pieces do not equal that strength. Success removes all unrest in that region, gives Commander one trophy, and if it defended against a normal primary Invasion also removes one attacker tower if possible. Excess strength of an indivisible alliance is explicitly unresolved in the summary; do not assume whether it matches. If Commander vacant, Military Affairs acts, or Chairman if that office is vacant, choosing defense pieces without trophies.
answers.evidence: Events in India — Attacks on Company; printed defense test and unresolved source gap

answers.answer: A vote at support −1 or less fails: discard law, resolve a dilemma’s If Failed text, return Opposition Leader token and give PM dial to that player; new PM moves proposed policy one adjacent space either way and resolves that policy. Zero or more passes: place law with passed laws, give PM passed-law token, resolve selected policy, then immediate law effects. After either result, restore all used vote cards to regular orientation. If the law causes Company failure, finish the vote before scoring.

In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, PM may call the special vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. Use ordinary voting/support threshold with exceptions: there is no policy; failure neither removes PM nor discards Deregulation, and PM may vote against. If it passes, lower Debt one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, give PM a passed-law token and activate firms. If it fails, increase Company-share scoring value one step by the Court VP token, to maximum ±3. 1813 starts deregulated.

To form a firm, a player managing none contributes an eligible Company share (not Chairman’s) or flips a workshop to invested, flips their family board to firm charter, places a family member as first firm share, sets Value to leftmost space, and takes £5 from bank into London. To invest, get manager consent and contribute a Company share or workshop; take £5 from bank into London. At most ten shares; excess investments still add £5 but make no share. Cannot use Company shares when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, nor shares created this turn even if traded away. Chairman share is ineligible. Invested workshops never revert, pay no bonus or Company-failure VP, and stay invested after firm failure.

Each firm with at least one ship gets exactly one trade attempt per turn and may choose a trade zone/home port, including a closed home port, or Hobnob. Simultaneously choose secret strategies, commit secret London bid; reveal bids but keep cards facedown until the matching Presidency starts. There each matching firm reveals, rolls one die per £1 bid and pays bid to bank; at least one 1/2 enables trade. Initiative is ship count minus successful dice. A President’s successful Trade creates its initiative; lowest initiative fills first, President choosing ties. If no successful President Trade or President vacant, firms go after Commander/Governor opportunities; Chairman breaks ties. Fill only open orders, up to ships + 1, starting home and tracing own route. Each order once per firm; can refill orders filled by another this turn. Repeat fills pay half listed revenue, rounded down. Advance firm Value one per full £6 added to India treasury this turn.
answers.evidence: Deregulation — Firm strategies and competing trade

answers.answer: At Revenue, firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or firm Value, using London and/or India treasuries. If insolvent, dissolve unless rescued: shares go to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships to matching shipyards, charter to family side; invested workshops stay invested. Rescue by emergency investment under normal share/workshop rules, or emergency merger with one other firm (which first pays its own expenses, then covers the endangered firm’s unpaid expenses). After expenses, manager may dividend only from India: each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 manager. A shareholder may waive their payout only with manager’s consent. Record actual total cash paid with dividend cube; active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero, Hobnob retains old marker. Sweep remaining India funds to London.
answers.evidence: Deregulation — Firm expenses, rescue and dividends

answers.answer: Components are limited, so when supply runs out do as much as possible; cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. All information including discards and family cash is public, except facedown blackmail and temporarily concealed firm strategies/bids during selection.

Negotiable: enterprises, facedown blackmail, family cash, Company/firm shares and promise cards. Not negotiable: officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, PM dial or Chairman piece. To transfer a share, return old owner’s member and replace it at that share location with a member from receiving family; adjust VP when luxury ownership changes. Blackmail can be traded facedown; once used it is faceup and cannot be traded.

Immediate transfers are binding; promises of future behavior are not, except printed promise card guaranteed effects may be called if possible. Calls follow the card’s timing and limits, and no promise calls are allowed during Final Scoring. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, guarantor chooses which to fulfill. Promise cards may be traded to a third party or back to guarantor. Transferred resources cannot activate twice (for example, a workshop paid this Bonus phase will not pay again after sale during that phase).

For five players add three extra setup cards; for six add six, then shuffle and deal evenly. Each player takes the listed cash, enterprises and positions; place holdings according to type: cash/enterprise in area, office member in listed office and matching card to owner, share member in Court, writer/officer/trainee in indicated box, Commander in Army Commander slot without office card, shipyard and ship with ship in listed sea zone or on yard if unfitted. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Deal three cards for London Season display, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown.

Game ends at scenario’s final turn or Standing failure. Failure is normally immediate; if during Events in India, finish that phase before scoring; if caused by legislation, finish the vote. Once game over, stop negotiations, promise calls and blackmail unless card explicitly permits final-scoring use. No negotiations or promise calls during all Final Scoring.

Power total is power from current track (bottom two positions count zero), +1 per passed-law token and trophy, +2 for PM, plus printed card power (blackmail faceup/down and applicable spouse). Awards for first/second are 3/1 VP on final turn 1–3, 5/2 on turn 4–6, 8/4 on turn 7–8. A tie for first means each tied player gets only the lower award and no other award; tied second gets none. Highest final VP wins; tie breaks by most windows, then clockwise from PM.

With survived Company, add current Court VP value per Company share; with failed Company, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. Before either outcome branch, each shareholder may make one eligible special retirement from supply, whether Company survived or failed; firm retirement is not replaced by failure card. Then survived: roll office attrition and retire Pensioners with no display cards. Failed: instead draw one random Company failure card and resolve it. Separately score all each player’s firm shares across firms, round that total down once, then subtract one VP per own Debtor’s Prison piece.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions — firm scoring and Company outcome

answers.answer: Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred. Take required enterprise/share trades immediately upon taking spouse. Retirement discounts are personal, can stack, and each is usable once per London Season and once during Final Scoring.

If returned because of Violet Effingham or unpaid tax, a fitted ship remains in play. That shipyard cannot be purchased while its matching ship is still in play; it becomes purchasable after the ship returns.

Purchase Luxury costs £4 to bank: take luxury, gain 2 VP while owned and its window icon; it is social enterprise. Purchase Shipyard costs £2 to bank: take yard and matching ship unfitted on it; shipping enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. Purchase Workshop costs £5 to bank: take workshop; manufacturing enterprise, two votes, £1 bonus, and 1 VP if Company fails unless invested. Seek Share places member on empty Stock Exchange space and pays bank £2/£3/£3/£4/£5 by queue position; it is applicant until issued as share. Enlist Writer places member in a Presidency Writers box, plus one extra once this turn with at least four vacant offices. Enlist Officer places member in Officers-in-Training.

If you must place a family piece and have none in supply, take one from any of your prizes and lose that prize’s printed VP; applies also to firm-share creation. If no family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.

If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns as Chairman, using a member from supply or, if needed and possible, a prize (lose that prize’s VP). If neither source can provide a piece, there is no Chairman.

Chairman is elected by shareholders. Chairman chooses Director (current officeholder other than Chairman/Governor; if all offices vacant, any writer), Manager of Shipping (any writer), and Military Affairs (Presidential Commander, else any officer, else trainee). Director chooses President (writer or associated Governor); associated President chooses Governor (writer or officer in region, not Commander). Chairman chooses China Superintendent (any writer; hired immediately on creation). Governor General replaces Director and is hired same way.

Director may make repeated Special Envoy checks, paying £1 from treasury per die, no penalty. Success either opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China by placing Superintendent overlay/card and immediately having Chairman hire a writer. After Envoys, Director may make up to two transfers, each one writer or ship between any Presidencies/sea zones, including China once created. No transfer while still taking Envoys.

Military Affairs may first make up to two transfers, each an officer or regiment between Armies, remaining in top half. Then assign every Officer-in-Training to any Army’s top half. Finally appoint Commanders: if vacant or another family has more total family pieces in the Army than incumbent’s family, choose among families with the most pieces; move chosen officer to Commander slot and return previous Commander to top as officer. A tie with incumbent’s family does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.

Each President chooses order of own Commander, Governors and Trade; Commander/Governors may decline, and each position completes all actions before next, with no interruption. Trade may go before/after them. If President vacant, Chairman sets order only and cannot trade or approve local alliance purchases.

Trade ships do not exhaust. Writers on orders return to their associated Presidency’s Writers box at Refresh, using dividers to keep affiliation straight; filled tokens and Presidency dividers return to supply.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade; Upkeep and Refresh

answers.answer: At start of Commander operations, before Deploy, request President treasury funds for printed-price local alliances; President must approve. Move purchased alliance active/top. Deploy or defense exhausts whole alliance to bottom; printed strength cannot be split and can be used once that turn for one purpose. Refresh exhausts unused active alliances too; unlike officers/regiments, alliances do not reactivate.

Company defense penalty is zero. Because no tower remains, there are no tower trophies. With no tower or faceup loot modifier, loot minimum is surviving participating officers plus £1 for Commander; distribute normally.

Build takes two successes total: first successful Build places partial ship in Governor’s region; a later successful Build completes it into the sea zone associated with Governor’s President. Each success performs just one stage. A commissioned regiment goes to the Army of that Governor’s President, with officer-like strength, loot paid to bank, and no officer-loss rolls.

China is created by successful Special Envoy or Envoy to China law; in both cases Chairman immediately hires any writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping/Director may send ships there as to any sea zone; it acts after Bengal. China ships count as Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws.

China gets only one Trade attempt per turn including failed attempt, so no retry. If no export icon in Company-controlled regions, do not attempt. Roll one die per ship. On success, count export icons only in Company-controlled regions: Company Balance gets £4 per icon and Superintendent’s family gets £1 per icon from bank. No non-Company exports count.

When Governor General law creates office, make Governors pensioners, remove overlays and partial Company ships, and return Governor/Director cards to box. Replace Director with Governor General preserving holder and fatigue and place ribbon overlay. Future conquests create no Governor/overlay; printed Company symbols indicate control. On region loss skip Governor Elimination.

First add £3 Balance per Company region. Then may Govern repeatedly, paying £1 from treasury per die, no penalty, at most one successful Govern per turn. Every 6 rolled adds one unrest to each Company region even on success; failure adds another unrest to every Company region. Success bonus is £1 per Company region and requires one benefit per region: complete Company ship into any sea zone (including China), regiment into any Army, or £2 to Balance/any office treasury except own, adding unrest to a Company region. Multiple Tax choices this turn must put unrest in different regions.

Roll storm die, then for rolled zone(s) roll once per player-owned ship: 1–2 nothing, 3–4 fatigue or sink if already fatigued, 5–6 sink. Company and extra ships are exempt. Sunk ships return to their shipyard unfatigued. China ships count Eastern. Firm ships use their strategy zone; Hobnob ships are exempt.

When an order closes, return any writer there to its owner’s supply and flip a filled token to closed. If told to close an order in an already fully closed region, Cascade by closing all open orders directly connected to that region’s orders. If a connected order is already closed, close that region’s northernmost open order instead; if none open, it also Cascades. A region initiates Cascade only once per event tile but can receive effects of multiple Cascades.
answers.evidence: Events in India — Closing orders and Cascades

answers.answer: Turmoil closes the northernmost open order in the region shown by the back of the new top draw-stack tile; if all closed, Cascade. Windfall pays owners £1 per writer on orders in that top-stack region and every bordering region. Shuffle: March Elephant, shuffle this tile into remaining draw stack, then separately shuffle discards and place on top. If draw stack was empty, March last instead.
Leader: in top-stack sovereign region add one tower; if dominated, instead rebel with printed explosion modifier. March only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.

Peace with Elephant on a border opens orders connected across its border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. If Elephant is wholly inside a region instead open all its orders and remove its unrest. Then March in either case.

Invasion succeeds only if attacker’s entire empire strength plus modifier is strictly greater than defender’s entire empire strength; equality does not win. Success replaces defender’s flag with attacker’s dominated flag; taking capital shatters whole defender empire. If attacker had no empire, use a free capital/star and matching small flag; if no flags available, no new empire/flags form. On failure attacker loses one tower.

Rebellion compares only rebelling region strength plus modifier with its sovereign capital’s strength; other empire regions do not count. It must be strictly greater, so tie fails. On success actor becomes sovereign, its flag is removed and all its orders close (Cascade if already closed). On failure remove one tower from capital.

On Company Region Loss, Commander returns half their family’s trophies rounded up and Commander member returns to supply. Roll once per associated Army officer; each 6 removes officer. Return Governor card to unused stack, fatigue/member to supply; remove overlay, partial Company ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion’s specified strength) and appropriate flag. Return control token symbol-side up, £ loot side down; region loses Presidency association. Invasion Crisis closes all orders (or Cascades if already closed); Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss escalates by regions lost so far this turn: first −1, second an additional −2, etc. Other Company regions are not automatically lost; attack and defend each separately.

After successful Invasion Crisis, move Elephant to the successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); other Marches use top-stack region. Put it fully inside a Company region. In dominated region point toward sovereign. In sovereign region point across shape-marked border; if neighbor already dominated by actor, choose first clockwise neighbor not so dominated. If all neighbors are, use redirect-arrow shape border pointing toward empire capital.

Roll storm die for targets: West→Bombay, South→Madras, East→Bengal; all storms means each region, none means top-stack region. For each target roll ordinary die for attack and resolve Invasion/Company attack. Successful attack closes all orders, or Cascades if already all closed; removes target flag and all matching flags if capital; restores dome if Company-controlled; sets tower strength to half attack die rounded down. March with circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded. Unrest does not increase primary attack or tower strength.
answers.evidence: Events in India — Foreign Invasion; FAQ & Rulings

answers.answer: PM must draw at least one law, revealing one at a time. After one or two ordinary non-dilemma draws, PM may stop or continue up to three total, then choose any revealed law and discard others. A dilemma forces its selection and ends drawing immediately. Before voting, PM moves dial arm clockwise or counterclockwise to the first policy space matching chosen law’s bottom icon; that space sets target and consequence.

Tax makes each family pay £1 to bank per target it owns; unpaid targets return to supply, including Chairman. Window tax also charges each window on enterprises and prizes; unaffordable enterprise/prize member returns. Bonus pays family £1 per target owned from bank. Power swaps target’s marker with next higher marker; if already highest, swap any other pair.

Starting with PM and clockwise, each player casts votes, paying £1 family cash per vote plus printed card votes. Each card’s votes can be used only once in whole vote, across rounds; rotate when used and restore after resolution. PM may call another full round or stop after each; a round with no votes must end voting.

A supporter may later oppose; once opposed, cannot vote for during this vote. Track opposition votes; biggest opponent holds Opposition Leader, ties retain current holder. With recipient consent, votes may be cast for someone already opposed or committed to oppose and add to that person’s opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except forced “Vote with my enterprises” promise.

Yes, final-turn upkeep is paid. Pay printed upkeep separately per prize member; unpaid member returns and lose its printed VP. While game continues, help can be negotiated. Nonfinal Refresh: writers return to associated Presidency Writers box; filled tokens and Presidency dividers to supply; extra ships to supply; exhausted Army officers/regiments reactivate; active alliances exhaust and do not reactivate; fitted player ships keep fatigue. Then advance turn.

Each shareholder may make one additional London Season retirement from supply, regardless of how many firms they own. Actual spend after spouse discounts must not exceed the highest total dividend marker among firms where they own a share; printed prize cost may exceed marker if discounts cover difference. No retirement from a firm with absent or zero marker. Otherwise normal retirement and prestige eligibility. At Final Scoring, score firms first, then allow one special retirement regardless of Company success/failure, before normal final-scoring steps and with no display cards.

Investment: £5 comes from bank into firm London. Trade revenue goes to India. Ship fitting and trade bids are paid from London; fitting £3 to bank. Expenses may use either treasury. Dividends are paid from India only. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries.

Firms phase follows Family share creation and precedes Hiring. Investments happen without set order until nobody wants more; manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm and PM resolves conflicts between firms. Strategies are then chosen.

A firm fitting a ship from a shipyard pays £3 from London to bank and needs yard owner consent. It may buy a player-owned ship already in Company with owner consent: unfatigued £3, fatigued £2, paid into Shipping treasury. It cannot buy Company ships or extra ships.

Only a player managing no firm may initiate hostile takeover; managing another firm disqualifies them. Get consent from holders of majority of target shares. Move firm ships, money and shares to their charter, copy both value/dividend cubes; former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.

Merger requires agreement by managers and every shareholder’s consent. Highest-value firm is primary; tied highest firms choose among themselves. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family sides. Negotiate transfers and any shares beyond ten with those owners’ consent. Entire agreement is one binding immediate transfer. Primary value/dividend track continues.
Hobnob means no bid, trade or dividends, but firm still pays expenses and retains prior dividend marker for retirement. Its ships are exempt from storms.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies and competing trade; expenses/dividends; Storms

answers.answer: Yes, emergency investment follows normal Company-share/workshop rules even at ten shares: contribution still brings £5 from bank into London but creates no additional share. For each emergency investment lower Value one space; use proceeds for expenses and lose any remaining cash. Shares created this turn remain ineligible for investment even if traded away.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends; Firms phase: investments

answers.answer: Emergency negotiated merger is limited to one other firm. Normal merger procedure still applies, including consent of every involved shareholder. Other firm must first pay its own expenses if not already paid, then cover endangered firm’s unpaid expenses.

Voluntary dissolution requires consent of all shareholders and uses insolvent-firm dissolution: shares to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships return to matching shipyards, charter flips to family side. Invested workshops remain invested for rest of game.

For each player, add VP from all of their shares across all firms, then round that player’s total down once; then subtract one VP for each of their family pieces in Debtor’s Prison. Firm score applies regardless of Company outcome and is counted separately from Company-share/workshop branch. Firm Value track VP per share: 1=−1; 2=0; 3–4=½; 5–7=1; 8–9=1½; 10=2.
Prizes: cost £2, upkeep £0, 0 VP, 0 windows; £4, upkeep £1, 2 VP, 1 window; £8, upkeep £2, 4 VP, 2 windows; £14, upkeep £3, 8 VP, 3 windows; £20, upkeep £4, 12 VP, 4 windows.

1710 starts turns 1–5 and has no deregulation procedures. 1758 turns 3–7, begins with monopoly and deregulation may be voted in. 1813 turns 5–8 and starts deregulated. Long 1710 turns 1–8, same initial position as 1710 with deregulation available.

1710: Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, £3 each office treasury, Royal Protection, one regiment per Army and no Company ships. 1758: Standing £12 expectations, Debt 3, £4 each treasury, Calico Acts, one regiment per Army, one Company ship in East Indian, and Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.

1813: turns 5–8; Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, £3 each treasury; laws Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor’s Prison side), Calico Acts; two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. Put +2/−2 share-value token in Court, create China, place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in their Presidencies, return Governor General law to box, overlay over Director of Trade; use Governor General instead of Director and no Governors. Exact map follows scenario card reverse.
Final turn 1–3: first/second power awards 3/1 VP; turns 4–6: 5/2; turns 7–8: 8/4. Tied first gives each tied player only the lower award and no other award.

Initial Power: Social 2, Company shares 1, Shipping 0, Manufacturing 0. Deregulation spaces line Standing £4/£6/£8 with Debt 5/6/7/8; Standing £4 and Debt 8 are starred. In relevant scenarios PM may call when Standing and/or Debt on lined space and must when either on starred space. Standing reset S is above £10.
answers.evidence: Setup — Power and Deregulation positions; Deregulation

answers.answer: No. Unrest does not increase Foreign Invasion primary attack strength or resulting tower level. Use ordinary attack die for attack and for halving to create towers. On success close all target orders once; if already all closed, Cascade. Region Loss does not close them again.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings — Foreign Invasion and unrest

answers.answer: If Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reduces a check to zero dice, it is failure. Company Fraud at start of Revenue rolls one die per your officeholder, reduces Balance by twice highest roll (minimum zero), and takes from bank only cash equal to actual Balance reduction. Public Demands Impeachment returns member to supply and office card to Vacant Offices. Military Oversight’s demoted Commander is eligible as an officer for reappointment.

Set board and supplies, shuffle India events, put local alliances in named Army boxes, set Company Balance to £5, Power tokens to indicated starting positions, family VP markers at zero, and loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. Follow chosen scenario setup card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and India political map. Put Turn marker on scenario’s starting date and PM dial arm on matching date.

Turn order: London Season → Family → Firms if deregulated → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. Eligible special Deregulation vote happens at very start before London Season. Skip London Season on game’s first turn.

If Chairman vacant, begin with former Chairman; then clockwise. Each player may retire each pensioner to a prize, paying printed cost and moving member to prize for printed VP. Spending is set aside until London Season ends to establish selection order, then paid to bank. Pensioners need not all retire, but unused ones do not stay for another turn: return them to supply after display selection.

No. Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove surviving capital’s starred flag; it ceases to be an empire. This applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest of the last dominated region.
